name: Aperture iris (bladed) transition

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-4, 2026-11-26): a photo-print film opens on a bladed aperture and closes its last picture with a hexagonal iris.

technique: A camera-aperture shape (six blades, a hexagon at the centre) closes over the frame to a point on black, or opens from a point onto the next scene. For a photography or camera subject the transition is the subject's own mechanism, so it reads as motivated.
purpose: A motivated close or open for camera and photography subjects: the transition is the subject's own mechanism.
visual_behaviour: Six blades close over the frame to a point on black, turning as they move (or open from a point onto the next scene).
mechanics: clip-path polygon (6-8 vertices) centred on the subject; radius from the half-diagonal to 0 over 0.1-0.3 s with power2.in to close, 0 to full with power2.out to open; rotate the polygon 30-60 deg during the move to suggest blades; a dark rim with faint blade lines.

decomposition.timing: Close 0.1-0.3 s (reference 26.46-26.56 s); the opening at 2.6 s shows the blade pattern as a still before it opens.

parameters.name: rotate
parameters.description: Degrees the polygon turns during the move

use_cases: A chapter close on a dark hold
failure_modes: Outside a camera context it is a gimmick
A plain circle reads as a generic iris; the blades make it an aperture

implementation.approach: clip-path polygon (6-8 vertices) centred on the subject; radius from the half-diagonal to 0 over 0.1-0.3 s (power2.in) while the polygon turns 30-60 degrees; reverse with power2.out to open; a dark rim with faint blade lines. Studio.fx.iris (effect iris-transition) does the circle; the bladed polygon variant is not built. Kept as a technique record rather than a note on the effect because effects carry no reference provenance.

provenance.observed: A dark circle with aperture blades opens onto a photo (2.6 s); at the end a hexagonal iris closes over the picture to a point on black in about 0.1 s (26.46-26.56 s).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
